pharm: Reversibly inhibits the chymotrypsin-like activity of the 26S proteasome, disrupting ubiquitin-mediated protein degradation and intracellular homeostasis, leading to cancer cell death
quick: 1.3 mg/m2 per dose, IV bolus or SC, on a cyclic schedule
Not applicable - injectable (IV bolus or SC)
Can cause fetal harm; use effective contraception
No clinically significant PK difference, including dialysis patients

summary: Bortezomib is an injectable (IV bolus or subcutaneous) proteasome inhibitor for adults with multiple myeloma or mantle cell lymphoma. The usual starting dose is 1.3 mg/m2 on a cyclic schedule. It has no boxed warning but carries important warnings including peripheral neuropathy, hypotension, cardiac and pulmonary toxicity, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES), GI toxicity, thrombocytopenia/neutropenia, tumor lysis syndrome, hepatic toxicity, thrombotic microangiopathy, and embryo-fetal toxicity. It is contraindicated in hypersensitivity to bortezomib, boron or mannitol and must never be given intrathecally (fatal).
indications: Treatment of adult patients with multiple myeloma
Treatment of adult patients with mantle cell lymphoma

dosage.d: 1.3 mg/m2 per dose as a 3-5 second IV bolus (1 mg/mL) or SC injection (2.5 mg/mL)
dosage.t: Cyclic schedule (e.g. twice weekly Days 1, 4, 8, 11 with rest); >=72 h between consecutive doses
dosage.n: IV and SC use only - never intrathecal; each route has a different reconstituted concentration

dosage.d: May restart at the last tolerated dose

admin: For IV or subcutaneous use only - do NOT administer by any other route
Contraindicated for intrathecal administration (fatal events have occurred)
Each route has a different reconstituted concentration (IV 1 mg/mL, SC 2.5 mg/mL) - use caution calculating volume
Administer IV as a 3 to 5 second bolus injection
Allow at least 72 hours between consecutive doses
Handle as a hazardous drug (gloves and protective clothing to prevent skin contact)
moa: Bortezomib is a reversible inhibitor of the chymotrypsin-like activity of the 26S proteasome, the protein complex that degrades ubiquitinated proteins. Proteasome inhibition prevents targeted proteolysis, disrupting multiple intracellular signaling cascades and normal homeostatic mechanisms, which leads to cancer cell death; it is cytotoxic to many cancer cell types and delays tumor growth in myeloma models.

absolute: Hypersensitivity (not including local reactions) to bortezomib, boron, or mannitol, including anaphylactic reactions
relative: Pre-existing severe peripheral neuropathy (treat only after careful risk-benefit assessment)
History of syncope, dehydration, or use of antihypertensives (hypotension risk)
Existing heart disease or cardiac risk factors
monitor: PRES - consider MRI and discontinue if suspected
Tumor lysis syndrome in high tumor burden

preg: Based on its mechanism of action and animal findings, bortezomib can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman; it caused embryo-fetal lethality in rabbits at doses lower than the clinical dose. Advise pregnant women of the potential risk to the fetus. Advise females of reproductive potential, and males with female partners of reproductive potential, to use effective contraception during treatment.
lact: There are no data on the presence of bortezomib or its metabolites in human milk or its effects on the breastfed child or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed child, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment.
renal: No clinically significant differences in bortezomib pharmacokinetics were observed based on renal impairment, including patients dosed after dialysis; no specific dose adjustment is given for renal impairment.
hepatic: Bortezomib exposure is increased in hepatic impairment. Use a lower starting dose in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment and monitor hepatic enzymes; interrupt therapy to assess reversibility if hepatic toxicity occurs.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inducers - decrease bortezomib exposure and may reduce efficacy; avoid concomitant use
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors - increase bortezomib exposure and toxicity risk; monitor closely and consider dose reduction
moderate: Antidiabetic agents - patients with diabetes may need close glucose monitoring and dose adjustment
minor: No clinically significant interaction with dexamethasone, omeprazole, or melphalan/prednisone
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor CBC and hepatic enzymes; consider MRI for suspected PRES

serious: Peripheral neuropathy (sensory, and sometimes severe sensory/motor)
Cardiac toxicity - new or worsening cardiac failure
emergency: PRES (visual or neurological symptoms - obtain MRI, discontinue)

monitoring: Complete blood counts (platelets and neutrophils) regularly throughout treatment
Signs and symptoms of peripheral neuropathy
Blood pressure (hypotension), especially with antihypertensives or dehydration
Cardiac status in patients with heart disease or risk factors
Tumor lysis syndrome in patients with high tumor burden
Visual/neurological symptoms suggesting PRES or thrombotic microangiopathy
counsel: Report numbness, tingling, burning or pain in the hands or feet (peripheral neuropathy)
Rise slowly and report dizziness or fainting (hypotension)
Report shortness of breath, swelling, chest pain, or visual/neurological changes promptly
Maintain adequate hydration and follow antiemetic/antidiarrheal advice for GI symptoms
Use effective contraception; females of reproductive potential and males with female partners should avoid pregnancy during treatment, and do not breastfeed
Keep all blood-count and clinic appointments
pk: Maximum 20S proteasome inhibition in blood ~5 minutes after dosing
IV Cmax ~112 ng/mL after 1.3 mg/m2 first dose; SC Cmax lower than IV with equivalent total exposure (AUC)
Mean elimination half-life ~76-108 hours after multiple 1.3 mg/m2 dosing
Reversible proteasome inhibition; given on a cyclic schedule with >=72 h between doses
Store vials at 25 C (excursions 15-30 C); retain in original package to protect from light
pearls: IV bolus or SC only - NEVER intrathecal (fatal); SC route reduces neuropathy with equivalent exposure
Peripheral neuropathy is dose-limiting - manage with dose modification or discontinuation
Watch for hypotension, cardiac failure, pulmonary toxicity, PRES and thrombotic microangiopathy
Monitor CBC for thrombocytopenia/neutropenia and watch for tumor lysis syndrome with high tumor burden
Lower starting dose in moderate-to-severe hepatic impairment; no adjustment for renal impairment/dialysis
No boxed warning, but embryo-fetal toxicity requires effective contraception
missed: Bortezomib is given by a healthcare professional on a scheduled basis. If you miss a clinic appointment, contact your oncology team to reschedule; at least 72 hours must elapse between consecutive doses.
overdose: There is no known specific antidote. Overdose has caused fatal outcomes associated with acute symptomatic hypotension and thrombocytopenia at more than twice the recommended dose. Monitor vital signs and provide supportive care.
